observation.visible_scene: A cream/white interior frying pan with a reddish-copper exterior and visible metal rivets sits on a black stovetop (a stove control knob marked '88' is at the lower right; a red pot edge is at the upper left). The pan holds a shallow pool of yellowish liquid with irregular white foam/froth patches floating on the surface, consistent with a gently heated fat or liquid. The pan and background remain fixed throughout, indicating a stationary camera.
visible_changes: The white foam patches slowly deform and reshape in place rather than translating across the pan: the left-of-center patch and the right-side patch change their outlines subtly frame to frame.
Small bubbles intermittently appear and pop along the lower edge and within the yellowish liquid, indicating gentle simmering/motion of the fluid surface.
The yellowish liquid shows slight internal swirling/convection, with bright specular highlights shifting as the surface moves.
No ingredients are added, no stirring occurs, and the pan does not move; the only motion is fluid-level deformation of foam and bubbles.
Camera position is essentially constant (rivets, pan rim, and stove knob keep the same screen positions), with at most minor handheld jitter.
outside_clip_unknowns: The identity of the liquid (melted butter, oil, or broth) and the heat setting are not established by the frames.
What precedes this excerpt (e.g., when the liquid was poured or heated) and what follows (e.g., whether it boils harder or ingredients are added) are unseen.
Whether the foam is protein/milk solids or another substance is not determinable from the clip.
uncertain_details: The exact cause of the foam's shape changes (convection vs. bubble bursting) is inferred from surface motion only.
Any very slight camera drift is ambiguous because the background is mostly static and close-cropped.
